Subject: PayGrid kickoff — runtime warmup, endpoint migration & rate governor

Hi team,

Following our discovery last week, PayGrid is ready to move from sandbox -> staged production. I want to align on three things we promised during the CSM -> implementation handoff:

1) SDK setup + quickstart snippets they can drop in (language: Go + Node)
2) Endpoint migration schedule (sandbox -> staging -> prod) and a minimal cutover checklist
3) Rate-governor defaults and recommended retry/timeouts to avoid early throttling on day-1 traffic

I attached an MLP (mutual_action_plan.xlsx) and a compressed snippet bundle (paygrid_sdk_snippets.tar.gz) with sample calls. Can Marcus and Vivek confirm the recommended timeout/retry matrix and any runtime warmup we should schedule (e.g., cache priming, KV warming, container warm pools)?

Target: a staged cutover window the week of 7/2.

Thanks — Monica

Subject: Re: PayGrid kickoff — runtime warmup, endpoint migration & rate governor

Monica — quick technical notes below (high level first, then config):

High-level:
- Recommend staging cutover in two phases: (1) traffic split 90/10 for 48 hours, (2) full switch after 72h of stability.
- Warmup: run 10 concurrent warmup calls for each model endpoint across the sequence-length matrix to populate KV cache. Expect ~30s cold-start tail in our GKE-based Dedicated pools if not primed.

Retry/Timeout matrix (recommended defaults):
- Client request timeout: 30s
- Connect timeout: 5s
- Retries on 5xx: up to 2 attempts, exponential backoff (base 200ms, max 2s)
- Retries on rate-limit (429): jittered backoff with Client-side token-bucket (burst 40, refill 20/sec)

Rate-governor: we should provision a soft limit for PayGrid in staging: 120 token-requests/sec total (aggregate across routes), with auto-failover to a lower-cost model variant on sustained 95th-percentile CPU. See attached rate_governor_config.yaml for values we typically start with.

Inline sample (Node) to show client-side token-bucket + retry (very small snippet):

const bucket = {tokens: 40, refillPerSec: 20};
async function makeCall(payload) {
  if (bucket.tokens <= 0) await sleep(50); // simple throttle
  bucket.tokens -= 1;
  try {
    const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify(payload),
      timeout: 30000
    });
    if (res.status === 429) throw new Error('RATE');
    return await res.json();
  } catch (err) {
    // implement exponential backoff + jitter here
    throw err;
  }
}

Attachments: included short glide samples and the YAML referenced. Happy to expand the snippet pack into language-specific packages.

—Marcus

Looping in a couple of operational guardrails from my side:

- Autoscale headroom: We'll reserve one warm node per model family for the first 72h after cutover to absorb bursty onboarding traffic. Ops should not scale this down automatically during that window.
- Observability: Please ensure PayGrid has access to the per-route latency and token cost dashboard. I'll provision a 14-day extended retention for this rollout (temporary).
- Fallback policy: If the primary model crosses CPU threshold or queue depth spikes, traffic will be routed to the smaller quantized variant with a clear flag set in response headers. We should list that behavior in the runbook for PayGrid engineering.

Action items for Monica:
- Confirm cutover target (Mon 7/2 morning or Tue 7/3?)
- Ask PayGrid for expected initial TPS distribution by route (sample CSV is ideal)

I'll also attach a short runbook snippet as part of the shared Drive link in a follow-up.

—Vivek

Subject: Re: PayGrid kickoff — runtime warmup, endpoint migration & rate governor

Thanks — Monica/Marcus/Vivek. A few clarifications from PayGrid engineering:

1) Endpoint names: our current sandbox uses /v1/paygrid/generate; in staging we want a separate hostname (staging-api.paygrid.com) mapped to your staging cluster. Is there a canonical approach on your side for hostname mapping + TLS?

2) Retry behavior: we prefer client-side retries only for idempotent enrichment calls; user-facing generate requests should avoid client retries and instead rely on graceful 429 handling (show a spinner + retry after header). Can you set the recommended headers we can detect to show the correct UX?

3) Cold-starts: What magnitude of latency delta should we expect for the unprimed sequence 1k token calls? We want to set SLAs in our SRE runbook.

We attached a nominal traffic CSV (expected_routes.csv) and flagged the top three high-volume routes.

From PayGrid: we prefer the cutover to be Tue 7/3 09:00 ET.

—Devon
